Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

phscs 0.3.0

New features

  • Added get_ptscs() for the Philippine Tourism Statistical Classification System (PTSCS). Choose the list with type = "industries" (default) or type = "products". It has no version, level, minimal or cols argument, and returns id, category_id, description and keywords instead of value and label. For industries keywords is a list column (split by comma); for products it is the original text.

Bug fixes

  • get_psced(): each level is now built from its own source file, so broad and narrow field labels match the published per-level lists. For levels 4 to 8, 5 broad field and 50 narrow field labels change; for example, broad field "60" is now “Social sciences, journalism and information” (was “Generic Programmes and Qualifications”). Codes are unchanged.

  • get_psccs(): sub-class "0103129" is listed twice in the source; its label is now “Other acts of robbery with homicide, n.e.c.”, matching the per-level source file (was “arson”).

  • get_pcoicop(level = "subitem") now returns the sub-item name as label (e.g. "Wheat") instead of repeating the code.

  • Labels that were blank in the source data now fall back to the first line of the description (PCOICOP 2020 groups 01.3, 02.3, 02.4, 03.2).

  • version can now be given as a number, e.g. get_psic(version = 2019).

  • get_psced(): the level column (with minimal = FALSE or cols = "level") now holds the education level code ("0" to "8") instead of the hierarchy depth (1 to 4).

  • Requesting a level that an edition does not have (e.g. get_pcoicop(version = "2009", level = "subitem")) now gives an error instead of an empty data frame.

  • Documentation for get_pcpc(), get_pcoicop(), and get_psccs() now states the correct default level ("all").

phscs 0.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-05-13

Breaking changes

  • get_psgc() has a completely new interface. It is now re-exported directly from the psgc package. The old parameters (token, version, level, harmonize, minimal, cols) are gone. Use the new psgc parameters instead:

    # Before
get_psgc(level = "regions")
get_psgc(grepl("^10", area_code))   # dplyr filter

# After
get_psgc(geographic_level = "region")
psgc_all <- get_psgc()
psgc_all[grepl("^10", psgc_all$psgc_code), ]   # base R subsetting

    See vignette("psgc", package = "psgc") for full documentation.

  • ... (dplyr filter) removed from all classification functions. get_psic(), get_psoc(), get_pcpc(), get_psced(), and get_pcoicop() no longer accept unquoted filter expressions. Filter rows with standard R subsetting after the call.

  • token and harmonize parameters removed from all classification functions. Data is now always sourced from the bundled local dataset — no API access or internet connection is needed.

New features

  • Added get_psccs() for the Philippine Standard Commodity Classification System (PSCCS 2018).

  • All classification functions gain a cols = "description" option to include the full text description alongside value and label.

  • PCOICOP now ships both the 2020 (default) and 2009 editions. Switch with get_pcoicop(version = "2009").

Other improvements

  • Removed runtime dependencies on dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, and jsonlite. The only Imports are now cli and psgc.

  • Minimum R version lowered from 4.1.0 to 3.5.

  • Data is pre-parsed at build time into a compressed sysdata.rda, making all functions substantially faster.
